title: Probe-Commit Arbiter: kernel-aware speculative handoff with tiered rollback
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a Probe-Commit Arbiter that performs lightweight prefill probes on lower-cost kernel/model variants, computes an acceptance score using model-internal heuristics (logprob delta, token entropy, prefix alignment), and either commits the speculative output or gracefully rolls back to a safe decode path. Goal: reduce median and p95 latency for typical chat workloads while keeping rollback frequency below target thresholds and avoiding semantic regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Arbiter can schedule a prefill probe and obtain an acceptance score within configured time budget (<= 12ms extra on fast-path)
Telemetry emitted: acceptance_score, probe_latency, commit_latency, rollback_count, kernel_switch_count, and model_mismatch_flag
End-to-end median latency improvement >= 8% and p95 improvement >= 5% on benchmark workload compared to baseline without speculative handoff
Rollback frequency <= 1.5% for production prompt set (canary) and false-accept rate quantified and below threshold
No semantic regression observed on 200 curated eval prompts (quality delta within noise bounds)
notes: Core idea: run a short prefill on an opportunistic variant (quantized or smaller model variant) that returns an initial hypothesis plus lightweight confidence metrics
Use attention-hook compatibility checks to ensure KV-cache layout and kernel expectations match before commit; if incompatible, force fallback path
Kernel selection logic: prefer quantized kernels that match model topology and sequence length profile of probe; fall back to fp16 kernel when alignment uncertain
Scheduling: prefer colocated probes on the same GPU to avoid cross-device transfer when capacity allows; otherwise use regional routing with soft-fallback to local decode

Fallback modes: soft-commit (continue decode on authoritative model while keeping probe output if acceptance is high), hard-rollback (discard probe and restart decode on authoritative model), and degraded mode (serve shorter confident prefix and complete with authoritative model)

decisions: Acceptance score will be a weighted composite: 0.6*logprob_delta + 0.3*token_entropy_inverse + 0.1*prefix_alignment
Kernel compatibility pre-check added: probe only commits if attention-hook mask and KV shape match authoritative runtime expectations
Circuit-breaker policy: disable probes if overall GPU utilization > 85% for more than 30s or rollback_rate > 2.5% over last 500 requests
